groups.heading: config: hosts was REJECTED, now ACCEPTED
groups.why: The merged build accepts zoned IPv6 strings in `hosts` that zod 3 rejected (2459::52d2%lo0, ::%1, 2001:db8::ff00:42:8329%25, a644::8654%eth0, 5ac3::de2a%wlan0 all: zod3 reject, merged accept). zod 3 accepted a %zone suffix only on lowercase fe80: addresses: fe80::1%eth0 and fe80::abcd%wlan0 passed zod 3 while fe81::1%eth0, 2459::52d2%lo0 and ::%1 were rejected by zod 3; the merged build accepts a zone on all of those addresses. Judgement: the zone-restore in src/schemas.ts is therefore not the 'reproduces exactly the set zod 3 matched' change the earlier sign-off claims (review/corpus-diffs.md, read directly rather than probed) -- it is wider than zod 3 AND wider than zod 4, so host strings that both versions used to refuse now flow into downstream connect/allow-list code. Judgement: a human must act before shipping -- either narrow the zone branch to fe80::/10 link-local (what zod 3 matched) or accept the widening deliberately and record it.

groups.heading: config: timeoutMs was ACCEPTED, now REJECTED
groups.why: zod 3 accepted timeoutMs = Infinity and stored Infinity; the merged build rejects it ('timeoutMs: Invalid input: expected number, received Infinity'). The value zod 3 stored does not survive JSON serialisation -- JSON.stringify({timeoutMs:Infinity}) contains null, not a number. Infinity is also not a JSON token (JSON.parse of Infinity throws) and only arrives from a numeric overflow literal such as 1e999. Finite values and the omitted-field default are unchanged: both builds store 5000. Judgement: an infinite timeout is not a usable configuration -- zod 3 was silently accepting a value that cannot round-trip to the config store -- so the tightening fails closed at the boundary and needs no action before shipping; the 463 hits reflect the fuzzer's generator preferring Infinity, not production traffic. Judgement: optional follow-up, give timeoutMs a real bound (e.g. .max(...)) so the message is about timeouts rather than IEEE-754 -- same shape of follow-up as the age case.

claims.claim: zod 3 accepted timeoutMs = Infinity and stored Infinity; the merged build rejects it with 'expected number, received Infinity'.
The value zod 3 stored does not survive JSON serialisation: JSON.stringify({timeoutMs:Infinity}) yields null in place of the number.
Infinity is not a JSON token (JSON.parse of it throws) and only reaches a parser from a numeric overflow literal such as 1e999, which parses to Infinity.
A finite timeoutMs is accepted by both builds and stores 5000 in both.

groups.heading: signup: ip was REJECTED, now ACCEPTED
groups.why: Same root cause as the hosts group, on the signup boundary: the merged build accepts signup ip values zod 3 rejected (305b:7432:e22d:4c35:1962:71c6:ed4d:69ae%1, 3d62::9037%1, 2001:db8::ff00:42:8329%25, ::%1, e575::ec0a%en0). On the ip field zod 3 accepted a zone only on lowercase fe80: addresses -- fe80::1%eth0 and fe80::abcd%wlan0 passed, while FE80::1%eth0, fe81::1%eth0, 3d62::9037%1 and ::%1 were rejected -- so the merged refine is wider than zod 3, not a restoration of it. The widening is bounded: an empty zone (fe80::1%), an IPv4 left part (1.2.3.4%eth0), junk (zzz%eth0) and a missing address (%eth0) are still rejected by both builds. Judgement: a human must decide whether global unicast addresses with a zone index are acceptable stored identities (a zone is only meaningful for link-local), and either narrow the refine to fe80::/10 or sign the widening off explicitly; the uppercase-FE80 case also shows the old check was case-sensitive, which is worth deciding on purpose rather than inheriting.

On the ip field zod 3 accepted a zone suffix only on lowercase fe80: addresses (fe80::1%eth0, fe80::abcd%wlan0 passed; FE80::1%eth0, fe81::1%eth0, 3d62::9037%1, ::%1 were rejected), while the merged build accepts all of them.
The zone branch still rejects an empty zone (fe80::1%), an IPv4 left part (1.2.3.4%eth0), junk (zzz%eth0) and a missing address (%eth0) in both builds.

groups.heading: signup: age was ACCEPTED, now REJECTED
groups.why: zod 3 accepted ages past the 53-bit mantissa (1e+21, 9007199254740994, 1e+30) and the merged build rejects them with 'Too big: expected int to be <=9007199254740991'. Such values are already lossy as doubles: 9007199254740993 === 9007199254740992 evaluates to true. Ages inside the representable range are unaffected: 13, 130 and 9007199254740991 are accepted by both builds. Judgement: none of the rejected values is a plausible age, nothing we stored above 2^53 was faithful, and this is exactly the change the earlier review signed off as ACCEPT NEW (review/corpus-diffs.md, read directly rather than probed) -- so no action is needed before shipping, beyond the already-noted follow-up of giving age a real domain bound.

groups.heading: signup: rejected by both, but different fields reported
groups.why: The verdict is identical in both builds -- only the list of reported fields differs. A signup with a bad id, bad email, bad plan and a zoned ip is rejected by both, with zod 3 listing [email,id,ip,plan] and the merged build [email,id,plan]; a signup with a bad email and age=1e+21 is rejected by both, with zod 3 listing [email] and the merged build [age,email]. Judgement: the two deltas are the ip field dropping out (the zoned-IPv6 widening already flagged MATTERS in the signup ip group) and the age field appearing (the unsafe-integer tightening in the age group), so fixing those groups fixes these lines too; the caller still gets the same rejection either way, so this group needs no separate action. Judgement: error messages/field order are not compared by the corpus harness, so no test churn is expected here.

groups.heading: signup: website accepted, but the PARSED VALUE changed
groups.why: Both builds accept the input; the only difference is surrounding whitespace. zod 3 stored the input verbatim (' https://example.com', 'https://example.com' plus a trailing newline) while the merged build stores the trimmed string, and ' https://example.com' and 'https://example.com' now collapse to the same stored value. Nothing else about the URL is rewritten: 'https://EXAMPLE.com/A?x=1', 'https://example.com/', 'https://example.com/a?x=1' and 'https://example.com' are stored unchanged by both builds, so there is no host lower-casing, no added trailing slash and no query rewriting. Judgement: leading/trailing whitespace is ignored by URL parsers anyway, so the trimmed value addresses the same resource and the change is a normalisation, not a semantic one -- no action needed before shipping. Judgement: the only residual risk is exact-string comparison or de-duplication of stored website values, which would see the trimmed form; that is low and can be handled after the fact.

claims.claim: For website ' https://example.com' and 'https://example.com' plus a trailing newline, both builds accept, zod 3 stores the input verbatim and the merged build stores the whitespace-trimmed string.
In the merged build ' https://example.com' and 'https://example.com' are stored as the same string.

URLs without surrounding whitespace are stored unchanged by both builds, including mixed-case host, trailing slash and query string ('https://EXAMPLE.com/A?x=1', 'https://example.com/', 'https://example.com/a?x=1', 'https://example.com').
